Doc describes only the is_read_shaped route to the result table/CSV; run_sql.py:78 also takes it when the frame carries the runner's read_result mark.

tool-scratch-storage.md lines 7/14 and transport.md line 123 tie the CSV/table route only to is_read_shaped; the read_result mark is a second route (pinned by test_rows_from_runner_with_other_dialect_are_kept).
transport.md line 123 omits the read_result route to the CSV write.
tools.md line 302 says query_type is "" when no keyword leads; first_sql_keyword (readonly.py:77-78) returns an unquoted identifier uppercased (foo bar -> FOO).
is_read_shaped docstring names only the SQL runners as caller; RunSqlTool.execute now also uses it.
TestSqliteRunnerCommentLedRowCap docstring only records past behavior.

read_result mark is one-sided and RunSqlTool.dialect (default None) is not tied to the runner's dialect; an embedder with mismatched dialects could see a rows_affected frame reported as a result table. build_agent wiring does not reach it.
No test runs a marked frame through RowCapRunner truncation; the mark survives only via pandas attrs propagation through iloc/copy.
_cte_reference_ids scope-analysis fallback logs at INFO with only the exception class name, though it can hide a user's data table.
first_sql_keyword returns "" on TokenError without logging; with read_only off a read sqlglot cannot tokenize is reported as row(s) affected with no trace.
Comment-led WITH ... UPDATE routing with read_only off (criterion text) is not pinned by a test; #316 tracks it.

report:
## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (no finding at or above the critical threshold; three checklist items inconclusive)
The change is ready to merge: every checklist item that could be settled by reading passed, and no reviewer raised a Critical finding.
Rule applied: rule 6 — findings below the threshold and INCONCLUSIVE checklist items remain → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major

1. No `changelog.d/324.<category>.md` fragment exists, although the change is visible to users: comment-led, parenthesis-led, CTE-led and `SELECT*` reads now return rows instead of a row count, `query_info["query_type"]` now skips leading comments, and `pyproject.toml` raises the install floor from `sqlglot>=25.0` to `sqlglot>=30.22`. CLAUDE.md asks for one fragment per applicable category. (raised by 1/6 agents)

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (11)

<details><summary>11 items</summary>

1. `docs/internal/agent/tool-scratch-storage.md` lines 7 and 14 describe only the `is_read_shaped` route to the result table. `src/sqllens/agent/tools/run_sql.py` line 78 also takes that route when the frame carries the runner's `read_result` mark, so a statement the tool's own dialect does not call read-shaped can still get a table and a CSV. With `build_agent` the two dialects match, so the routes agree in shipped wiring. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: internal doc page; making it name the read_result route changes no output; git grep of .sh/.py/.jq/.yml/.toml/.github for tool-scratch-storage found no reader; docs/internal is not published -->
2. Same two lines of `docs/internal/agent/tool-scratch-storage.md` (lines 7 and 14), and `docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md` line 123, tie the CSV write only to `is_read_shaped`; the runner's `read_result` mark (pinned by `test_rows_from_runner_with_other_dialect_are_kept`) is a second route. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: internal doc pages; the sentences are true as non-exclusive statements and changing them changes no output; git grep of .sh/.py/.jq/.yml/.toml/.github found only a pointer from sql_threads.py docstring to transport.md, not a behavior reader; docs/internal is not published -->
3. `docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md` line 123 says the CSV is written when a read-shaped statement returns rows, without the `read_result` route. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: internal doc page; no tool reads it for behavior (git grep found only a docstring pointer in src/sqllens/agent/integrations/sql_threads.py:33); docs/internal is not published -->
4. `docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md` line 302 (modified by this diff) says `query_type` is `""` when no keyword leads the statement. `first_sql_keyword` (`src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` lines 77-78) returns an unquoted identifier uppercased, so `foo bar` gives `FOO`, not `""`. The function's own docstring states this correctly. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: the sentence describes first_sql_keyword output; correcting it changes no output, branch or covered set; git grep of .sh/.py/.jq/.yml/.toml/.github found only a docstring pointer in src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:683, not a reader; docs/internal is not published -->
5. The `is_read_shaped` docstring (`src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` lines 91-94) still names only the SQL runners as its caller; `RunSqlTool.execute` now also uses it to choose between a result table and a row count. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: docstring of an internal function not printed by the program; no tool reads it -->
6. The new `TestSqliteRunnerCommentLedRowCap` docstring (`tests/unit/test_safety_limits.py` lines 505-506) only records past behavior and does not say what a later change must keep. (raised by 1/6 agents)
7. The `read_result` mark is one-sided: `src/sqllens/agent/tools/run_sql.py` line 78 treats an unmarked frame as "use the tool's own classifier", and `RunSqlTool.dialect` defaults to `None` and is not tied to the runner's hard-coded dialect. An embedder who builds `RunSqlTool` without `dialect` can get a runner's `rows_affected` frame reported as a result table; `build_agent` passes matching dialects, so shipped wiring does not reach this. (raised by 1/6 agents)
8. No test runs a marked frame through `RowCapRunner`'s truncation path (`src/sqllens/safety/limits.py` lines 96-98); the mark survives only because pandas copies `attrs` through `iloc[:cap].copy()`. (raised by 1/6 agents)
9. `_cte_reference_ids` (`src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` lines 164-172) logs a scope-analysis failure at INFO with only the exception class name. That fallback returns "introspection", which hides a data table from the user, so a sqlglot API change would leave little trace. (raised by 1/6 agents)
10. `first_sql_keyword` (`src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` lines 68-71) returns `""` on a `TokenError` without logging. With `read_only` off, a read SQLite runs but sqlglot cannot tokenize then reports "N row(s) affected" with no record of why. The `""` result itself is what the acceptance criteria require. (raised by 1/6 agents)
11. No test pins the routing of a comment-led `WITH … UPDATE` with `read_only` off (`tests/unit/test_safety_limits.py` lines 304-323); `test_is_read_shaped_by_dialect` covers only `WITH … SELECT`. Issue #316 tracks that routing. (raised by 1/6 agents)

</details>

  </details>

- VC-75: INCONCLUSIVE (critical) — `is_read_shaped("SELECT n FROM widgets # x\r'\n", "mysql")` is `True`, and `assert_select_only` accepts that statement with `dialect="mysql"`. [tests/unit/test_safety_limits.py:295]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Graded with criteria.json (criterion 6 matches the claim verbatim). Test test_mysql_carriage_return_in_line_comment (tests/unit/test_safety_limits.py:295-302) asserts exactly the claim: is_read_shaped(sql,'mysql') is True and assert_select_only(sql, dialect='mysql') does not raise. assert_select_only half traced: _mysql_parse_sql (readonly.py:543-556) ends a '#' comment only at '\n' and rewrites '\r' inside it to a space, so the later quote is inside the comment before sqlglot.parse; this half holds. The is_read_shaped half (readonly.py:45-96) passes the raw string to sqlglot's MySQL Dialect.tokenize; whether the pinned sqlglot>=30.22 (pyproject.toml:44) MySQL tokenizer keeps '\r' inside a '#' comment (so no TokenError -> '' -> False) lives in sqlglot's tokenizer source, which is not in the head view. I did not run pytest or read sqlglot's tokenizer, so that half is not settled by reading.

  </details>

- VC-83: INCONCLUSIVE (critical) — A statement `is_read_shaped` does not classify as read-shaped (for example `UPDATE` with `read_only` off) still gets the `row(s) affected` notification and no result table. [tests/unit/test_safety_limits.py:624]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  criteria.json counts (criterion 14 present, all elements are {criterion,text}). Test test_not_read_shaped_gets_rows_affected (tests/unit/test_safety_limits.py:619-638) runs UPDATE and 'SELECT n FROM widgets /* note' through SqliteRunner(read_only=False) with dialect=sqlite and asserts 'row(s) affected', a NotificationComponent and no 'results' metadata; run_sql.py:171-185 supports this (else branch emits the notification, metadata has only rows_affected/query_type). Condition split at run_sql.py:78 `is_read_shaped(args.sql, self.dialect) or df.attrs.get(READ_RESULT_ATTR)`: (a) is_read_shaped false -> trigger itself; (b) READ_RESULT_ATTR true is set only in limits.py:76 (rows_to_capped_df), which runners call only when their own is_read_shaped(sql, hardcoded dialect) is true. So when tool dialect differs from the runner's, a statement the tool does NOT classify read-shaped (e.g. '# c\nSELECT n FROM widgets', tool dialect None/postgres/sqlite, MySQL runner) gets a result table and no 'row(s) affected' -- a departure from the claim inside the trigger, pinned deliberately by test_rows_from_runner_with_other_dialect_are_kept (test_safety_limits.py:640-658). With matching dialects (build_agent uses sqlglot_dialect_for_url, readonly.py:99-110, same dialect as the runners) the alternative cannot fire. I could not settle whether a shipped caller or documented state constructs RunSqlTool with a mismatched dialect, so reachability is unsettled; not FAIL. The claimed tested cases themselves behave as claimed.

  </details>

</details>

checklist.evidence: Graded with criteria.json (criterion 6 matches the claim verbatim). Test test_mysql_carriage_return_in_line_comment (tests/unit/test_safety_limits.py:295-302) asserts exactly the claim: is_read_shaped(sql,'mysql') is True and assert_select_only(sql, dialect='mysql') does not raise. assert_select_only half traced: _mysql_parse_sql (readonly.py:543-556) ends a '#' comment only at '\n' and rewrites '\r' inside it to a space, so the later quote is inside the comment before sqlglot.parse; this half holds. The is_read_shaped half (readonly.py:45-96) passes the raw string to sqlglot's MySQL Dialect.tokenize; whether the pinned sqlglot>=30.22 (pyproject.toml:44) MySQL tokenizer keeps '\r' inside a '#' comment (so no TokenError -> '' -> False) lives in sqlglot's tokenizer source, which is not in the head view. I did not run pytest or read sqlglot's tokenizer, so that half is not settled by reading.

checklist.claim: A statement `is_read_shaped` does not classify as read-shaped (for example `UPDATE` with `read_only` off) still gets the `row(s) affected` notification and no result table.
checklist.evidence: criteria.json counts (criterion 14 present, all elements are {criterion,text}). Test test_not_read_shaped_gets_rows_affected (tests/unit/test_safety_limits.py:619-638) runs UPDATE and 'SELECT n FROM widgets /* note' through SqliteRunner(read_only=False) with dialect=sqlite and asserts 'row(s) affected', a NotificationComponent and no 'results' metadata; run_sql.py:171-185 supports this (else branch emits the notification, metadata has only rows_affected/query_type). Condition split at run_sql.py:78 `is_read_shaped(args.sql, self.dialect) or df.attrs.get(READ_RESULT_ATTR)`: (a) is_read_shaped false -> trigger itself; (b) READ_RESULT_ATTR true is set only in limits.py:76 (rows_to_capped_df), which runners call only when their own is_read_shaped(sql, hardcoded dialect) is true. So when tool dialect differs from the runner's, a statement the tool does NOT classify read-shaped (e.g. '# c\nSELECT n FROM widgets', tool dialect None/postgres/sqlite, MySQL runner) gets a result table and no 'row(s) affected' -- a departure from the claim inside the trigger, pinned deliberately by test_rows_from_runner_with_other_dialect_are_kept (test_safety_limits.py:640-658). With matching dialects (build_agent uses sqlglot_dialect_for_url, readonly.py:99-110, same dialect as the runners) the alternative cannot fire. I could not settle whether a shipped caller or documented state constructs RunSqlTool with a mismatched dialect, so reachability is unsettled; not FAIL. The claimed tested cases themselves behave as claimed.
